## [TypeScript Frontend: Hexagonal Architecture](../05-building-block-view/typescript.md)

- TS-ARCH-01: `domain`, `application` and `ports` MUST NOT import UI frameworks, routers, state libraries or HTTP clients.
- TS-ARCH-02: No business logic in components or templates.
- TS-ARCH-03: View-state stores are part of the UI adapter and follow TS-ARCH-08: they call use-case contracts only, never HTTP, adapters, outgoing ports, generated code or another store.
- TS-ARCH-04: Every backend call goes through an outgoing port implemented in `adapter/out/http`.
- TS-ARCH-05: Backend DTOs MUST NOT leave `adapter/out/http` (two-way mapping at the API boundary).
- TS-ARCH-06: Validate untrusted input at the boundary with schema parsing; the schema library is zod (default TS-D2).
- TS-ARCH-07: Ports are narrow (ARCH-ADP-08):
- TS-ARCH-08: The UI depends on use-case contracts from `ports/in`, not on use-case implementations (shared default D1), and never on outgoing ports (`ports/out`).
- TS-ARCH-18: The HTTP adapter turns error responses into domain errors, in one mapper per adapter (ARCH-ADP-05).
- TS-ARCH-09: Only the feature's composition file connects implementations to contracts.
- TS-ARCH-10: Features import each other only through `index.ts`.
- TS-ARCH-19: A feature uses another feature's use cases only through that feature's published API.
- TS-ARCH-20: `index.ts` never exports routes.
- TS-ARCH-11: `shared/ui` contains no feature or business logic and never imports from `features/`.
- TS-ARCH-12: Architecture rules are checked in CI with dependency-cruiser (or `eslint-plugin-boundaries`), with `tsPreCompilationDeps: true`.
- TS-ARCH-13: Guard against "checks nothing" (ARCH-ENF-02).
- TS-ARCH-14: Larger frontends may turn features into workspace packages/libraries (npm/pnpm workspaces, Nx) with explicit dependencies.
- TS-ARCH-15: Batching, request coalescing and caching of backend data live in the outgoing adapter, as a decorator implementing the same port (API-N1-04).
- TS-ARCH-16: Frontend use cases may return immutable frontend domain types (`readonly Order[]`) instead of use-case specific result models.
- TS-ARCH-17: Injection tokens (keys) live in `<feature>.tokens.ts`, which imports only the feature's `ports`.
- TS-ARCH-21: A new load supersedes the previous one, and every async result is applied to the current state.
- TS-ARCH-22: Frontend code reads the current time only from the platform's clock, and the business date only from one platform function (ARCH-UC-20).
- TS-ARCH-23: Stores and components catch only the errors they expect.

## [Generated API Clients (Orval)](../08-crosscutting-concepts/api/typescript-openapi-clients.md)

- TS-API-01: Orval generates clients, types, zod schemas and MSW mocks from the pinned spec:
- TS-API-02: Generated code is gitignored, never edited, and excluded from lint and coverage.
- TS-API-03: The client mode is one whose calls pass the platform HTTP stack.
- TS-API-04: Generated clients are not app-wide singletons.
- TS-API-05: The adapter parses every response with the generated zod schema before mapping (TS-ARCH-06).
- TS-API-06: The adapter maps to domain types and returns `Promise` (TS-D1), honoring the caller's `AbortSignal`:
- TS-API-07: Batching and caching (API-N1 S4/S5) are decorators in the same folder, implementing the same port and wrapping the plain adapter.
- TS-API-08: A spec change is reviewed together with its effect on the frontend:
- TS-API-09: `urlEncodeParameters: true` is set in every Orval client output.
- TS-API-10: Downloads of generated files (exports, reports) go through the outgoing HTTP adapter by default:

## [TypeScript Tooling](../08-crosscutting-concepts/development/typescript-tooling.md)

- TS-TOOL-01: `strict` is on, plus these checks.
- TS-TOOL-02: The supported browsers are the Baseline "widely available" browsers of a date the baseline fixes, and `lib` is the newest ECMAScript level all of them support.
- TS-TOOL-03: No `any`.
- TS-TOOL-04: ESLint flat config with this plugin set:
- TS-TOOL-05: Lint errors fail the build. No warnings policy:
- TS-TOOL-06: Disabling a rule inline requires a named rule and a reason (`// eslint-disable-next-line rule -- reason`), enforced by `@eslint-community/eslint-comments/require-description` and `no-unlimited-disable`;
- TS-TOOL-07: Known overlaps are resolved in the shared config, not per project:
- TS-TOOL-08: Prettier formats everything it supports (TS, HTML templates, SCSS/CSS, JSON, Markdown, YAML).
- TS-TOOL-09: CI runs `prettier --check` and `eslint`.
- TS-TOOL-10: Every TypeScript project offers the same script names, so humans, agents and CI don't have to guess:
- TS-TOOL-11: `.npmrc` sets `ignore-scripts=true`, `allow-git=none` (or `root`) and `min-release-age=7` (days; SEC-CI-02), CI installs with `npm ci`, and `package-lock.json` is committed with its diffs reviewed.
- TS-TOOL-12: CI scans the lockfile for known vulnerabilities and runs `npm audit signatures`;
- TS-TOOL-13: Dependencies are added deliberately (age, maintainers, install scripts, usage checked).
- TS-TOOL-14: The toolchain guarantees an npm that knows the `.npmrc` keys.
- TS-TOOL-15: Dependency updates are automated as a capability of the repository.
- TS-TOOL-16: Builds are reproducible.
- TS-TOOL-17: knip reports unused dependencies, exports and files, and `verify` runs it.
- TS-TOOL-18: `check` is the inner loop, `verify` the gate.
- TS-TOOL-19: `verify` and `check` run every step, report all failures together and fail at the end.
- TS-TOOL-20: E2E code is type-checked and linted inside `verify`.
- TS-TOOL-21: ESLint bans reading the wall clock outside the platform clock (TS-ARCH-22).

## [TypeScript: Browser Security](../08-crosscutting-concepts/security/typescript.md)

- TS-SEC-01: No tokens, session ids or personal data in `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, IndexedDB or URLs.
- TS-SEC-02: No `eval`, `new Function`, string-argument `setTimeout`/`setInterval`, `document.write`.
- TS-SEC-03: Navigation targets and redirects that come from user input are checked against an allow-list of internal paths.
- TS-SEC-04: Nothing secret is in the bundle or in environment files.
- TS-SEC-05: Production builds publish no source maps;
- TS-SEC-06: Client logging and error reporting scrub tokens, personal data and form values;
- TS-SEC-07: Third-party scripts, tags and fonts are avoided or self-hosted.
- TS-SEC-08: API data is validated at the adapter (generated zod schemas, TS-API) and never evaluated as code or inserted as HTML.
- TS-SEC-09: zod runs jitless in the browser.
- TS-SEC-10: Sign-out posts to the BFF's logout endpoint with the XSRF header, expects `200 {"redirectUri": …}` and then navigates the whole page there with `window.location.assign`.

## [TypeScript E2E: Matrix, Responsive, Themes, Screen Readers](../08-crosscutting-concepts/testing/typescript-e2e.md)

- TS-TEST-17: Viewports are Playwright projects named after the size class, defined once in `playwright.config.ts`.
- TS-TEST-18: The matrix is tiered, and this table is its only definition.
- TS-TEST-28: Tagged main states are re-scanned in the other theme conditions, in one browser and one viewport:
- TS-TEST-29: The matrix grows one dimension at a time from the default cell.
- TS-TEST-30: The pull-request tier has a wall-clock budget, recorded in the product's chapter 10 and enforced as the time limit of the pipeline job (default:
- TS-TEST-31: Retries only in CI, and a retried test is a defect.
- TS-TEST-32: A stubbed E2E test fails when the page makes an API call that no stub answers, throws an unhandled error, or reports a missing translation.
- TS-TEST-33: Run E2E at milestones while building, the full matrix once per delivered part.
- TS-TEST-19: A shared fixture asserts reflow and text spacing on every `@responsive` screen:
- TS-TEST-20: Each shell and each list-detail screen has a resize-transition test:
- TS-TEST-21: Target size (A11Y-10, A11Y-16) is asserted in the browser, and the axe fixture proves that `target-size` ran.
- TS-TEST-22: Visual regression is opt-in per project.
- TS-TEST-23: Assert accessible name, description and state through accessibility APIs, not ARIA attributes:
- TS-TEST-24: Status messages are asserted after the triggering action (A11Y-20):
- TS-TEST-25: The app shell and each main screen have a scoped, partial ARIA snapshot (A11Y-23):
- TS-TEST-26: Each main route has an E2E navigation test (A11Y-21), at the default cell:
- TS-TEST-27 (opt-in per project): Real screen reader smoke tests run nightly with NVDA on Windows for one to three critical journeys.

## [TypeScript Testing](../08-crosscutting-concepts/testing/typescript.md)

- TS-TEST-01: Test doubles are created with `mock<Contract>()` from `vitest-mock-extended`, typed by the port or use-case interface.
- TS-TEST-02: `vi.mock()` (module mocking) is not used for our own modules.
- TS-TEST-03: Stub queries with `calledWith(...).mockResolvedValue(...)`, verify only commands (TEST-TDD-09).
- TS-TEST-04: HTTP adapters are tested against MSW, using the handlers Orval generates from the spec (`get<Operation>MockHandler`) with per-test overrides.
- TS-TEST-05: Domain tests are plain functions in, values out.
- TS-TEST-06: Snapshot tests are not used for component output.
- TS-TEST-07: Component tests use Testing Library and query by role and accessible name (`getByRole('button', { name: 'Place order' })`).
- TS-TEST-08: Interactions use `@testing-library/user-event`, not synthetic `dispatchEvent`.
- TS-TEST-09: Every component test file runs axe on its main rendered states (A11Y layer L3):
- TS-TEST-10: Two tiers.
- TS-TEST-11: Locators by role, label or text, as in component tests.
- TS-TEST-12: Accessibility per main screen and state (A11Y layer L4, A11Y-27), through a shared fixture.
- TS-TEST-13: Keyboard journeys (A11Y layer L5):
- TS-TEST-14: Request budgets per main screen (API-N1-06):
- TS-TEST-15: No fixed waits (`waitForTimeout`).
- TS-TEST-34: Every E2E scenario arranges its own data and leaves nothing another run depends on.
- TS-TEST-35: An E2E test never waits out a business rule; it arranges the state through the API.
- TS-TEST-16: The stubbed tier runs in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit; the smoke tier may use Chromium only.
